Non-Surgical Tennis Elbow Relief: Top Treatments in Hyderabad

Dr. B Harsha Vardhana Reddy12 April 2026

Introduction

Tennis elbow, medically known as lateral epicondylitis, is a painful condition affecting the tendons around the elbow joint. Despite its name, it doesn't only afflict tennis players. In fact, it can affect anyone who engages in repetitive arm and wrist activities. If you're experiencing persistent elbow pain and are searching for effective treatment options without surgery, read on to learn more. Dr. B Harsha Vardhana Reddy, a renowned orthopedic surgeon at Apollo Hospitals, Financial District, Hyderabad, is here to guide you on non-surgical treatments for tennis elbow.

What is Tennis Elbow?

Tennis elbow occurs when the tendons in the elbow are overloaded, usually by repetitive motions of the wrist and arm. This leads to inflammation and tiny tears in the tendons, resulting in pain and tenderness on the outside of the elbow. Symptoms can also include a weak grip, stiffness, or a burning sensation in the elbow.

Common Symptoms and Diagnosis

  • Persistent pain and tenderness on the outside of the elbow
  • Weakness in the forearm
  • Difficulties in gripping or holding objects
  • Wrist pain that radiates down the forearm

If you're experiencing these symptoms, an orthopedic specialist like Dr. Harsha at Apollo Hospitals, Financial District, Hyderabad can accurately diagnose the condition through a physical examination and may use imaging tests like X-rays or MRI for further evaluation.

Treatment Options

Non-surgical treatments for tennis elbow are highly effective and encompass multiple strategies. Here are some of the widely recommended treatments:

Rest and Activity Modification: Limiting the activities that exacerbate the symptoms can help reduce strain on the elbow.
Physical Therapy: A physical therapist can guide you through exercises that strengthen and stretch the muscles around the elbow.
Ice Therapy: Applying ice packs to the affected area can help reduce inflammation and alleviate pain.
Medications: Over-the-counter pain relievers or anti-inflammatory medications may be recommended to manage pain and swelling.
Bracing: Wrist braces or forearm straps can provide support and help in distributing pressure across the forearm.
Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy (ESWT): This non-invasive procedure involves delivering shock waves to the affected area to promote healing.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Can lifestyle changes help manage tennis elbow?

A: Yes, lifestyle modifications such as proper ergonomic adjustments and activity breaks can significantly contribute to managing symptoms.

Q: How long does it typically take to recover from tennis elbow?

A: Recovery times vary but with consistent non-surgical treatment, many patients see improvement in a few weeks to several months.
